author: Dustin Nelson
title: Beloved First Avenue stage manager Conrad Sverkerson has died at 66 - NewsBreak
text:
By Dustin Nelson ,
1 hours ago The exterior walls of First Avenue, filled with white stars, are a Minnesota landmark. They tell a significant piece of the story of music in the Twin Cities. The names inside those stars include legends like Prince, storied local performers like Soul Asylum and Slim Dunlap, and, simply, Conrad.
Unlike most names on the wall, Conrad Sverkerson was an employee. He was the stage manager for First Avenue Productions and had been a recognizable face at the venue for nearly four decades.
Sverkerson died of lung cancer at age 66 on Tuesday, Sept. 30.
First Avenue/Facebook Since the venue shared the news, dozens of musicians from Minnesota and beyond paid tribute to someone who was often the first and last person an artist would see when playing First Avenue.
"Our communal First Avenue heart is shattered by the passing of our beloved Conrad Sverkerson," reads a message from First Avenue on social media.
"He helmed our ship for decades, working alongside some of his best friends and his brother, Billy. In typical Conrad fashion, he started his first night of work as a doorman and ended it playing foosball with Duran Duran."
The venue's statement echoes what many artists and fans have shared: that he was a familiar face for fans and artists, someone who cared, and often earned shout-outs from artists during performances.
The list of artists, friends, and other businesses that have posted fond memories online is almost as long as the list of musicians with whom he worked, including the Flaming Lips' Wayne Coyne, Dr. Dog, The Lemonheads, Pert Near Sandstone, The Hold Steady, Mason Jennings, Dusty's Bar , Electric Fetus , and dozens of others.
"You are etched into the fabric of First Avenue as much as each brick that layers its wall," wrote musician and talent booker Christy Costello. "I’m so happy I got to know you outside of those bricks and that we became friends."
One of very few stars dedicated to people who didn't perform on the stage (at least in the traditional way), the "Conrad" star at the venue is fittingly placed on the side door where Sverkerson loaded in hundreds of artists who were seen by thousands of music fans in Minnesota over the course of nearly four decades.
"To say that Conrad was the face of First Avenue for so many over the years would be an understatement," the venue's message continues. "Throughout his 37 years working here, Conrad's spirit has been indelibly woven into the very foundation of our star-studded building and we will work to honor it every show. We'll miss him every day. His legacy endures. Conrad forever."
Sverkerson died at Essentia Health-St. Mary's Medical Center in Duluth , surrounded by family and friends, per the Star Tribune . He's survived by his partner Dina Bizzaro and seven of his 10 siblings, as well as many nieces and nephews.
